📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Avengers: Doomsday" is going to be one of the biggest movies of the year, if not ever, that much is certain.
  • Indeed, the worst thing one can say about this film right now is that it looks exactly like what you would expect.
  • That being said, there is one notable reason to be excited about "Doomsday." No, not the X-Men (though their inclusion is certainly cool) or the return of Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Avengers: Doomsday" is going to be one of the biggest movies of the year, if not ever, that much is certain. But so far, the movie's marketing has been quite, well, underwhelming. We already had one "Avengers" film (well, two) that relied entirely on gathering lots of known Marvel Cinematic Universe characters on screen at the same time. To do that again feels less special, as exciting as it is to see Cyclops (James Marsden) leading the X-Men into battle here.

Indeed, the worst thing one can say about this film right now is that it looks exactly like what you would expect. It's massive, sure, but it doesn't feel surprising in any way. Marvel announcing Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom in the movie felt desperate, too, as it was obviously the studio's way of trying to win back the fans who'd been disappointed by the MCU's post-"Avengers: Endgame" output. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" aside, Marvel's no longer the reliable hit machine that it once was.

That being said, there is one notable reason to be excited about "Doomsday." No, not the X-Men (though their inclusion is certainly cool) or the return of Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen). Instead, it's the fact that "Doomsday" is technically a direct sequel to "Thunderbolts*," itself by far the best non-"Spider-Man" MCU movie since "Endgame." More specifically, it picks up where that film left off, with the titular team (also known as the West Chesapeake Valley Thunderbolts sponsored by Shane's Tire Tech giant) now officially being known as the Upcoming Avengers.

Sure enough, the final "Doomsday" trailer features a few shots of the New Avengers amidst all the new footage of Chris Evans as Steve Rogers, and it's enough to finally get me hyped for this film.

For the most part, the visuals in the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer look horrendously muted and dull, save for a single brief shot of David Harbour's Alexei Shostakov dressed in a horrendous New Avengers tracksuit staring in awe as Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) arrives at Avengers Tower. Immediately, the image both brightens the trailer and reminds you that as serious as "Doomsday" may be (with the old Avengers looking more tired and beaten up than ever), the New Avengers bring a whole different vibe to the table. After all, they're silly, not great at teamwork, and don't consider themselves to be gods. Instead, they talk through their psychological challenges and even hug it out like something out of "Neon Genesis Evangelion.".

Recent findings suggest that as the final trailer makes clear, "Doomsday" is all about different superhero groups coming together. You have the remnants of the original Avengers team, the X-Men, the Thunderbolts/Newly introduced Avengers, and the Fantastic Four — plus the stragglers from various MCU titles that we collectively kind of forgot about. Each brings a different dynamic to the film, with the New Avengers specifically being a group of loser superheroes and criminals not unlike the Guardians of the Galaxy ... with the substantial difference being that the former have to save themselves before they can save anyone else. It's why "Thunderbolts*" makes for such an emotional gut punch, especially when its leads come together as a team, and the idea of seeing them interact with the MCU at large does more to make "Doomsday" feel interesting than any number of cameos could.

"Avengers: Doomsday" will see the Fresh Avengers suit up alongside their companions when it hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, when we think of secrecy surrounding movies, naturally we think MCU, but the amount of secrecy that went into The Odyssey is insane.
  • According to recent reports, the actor portrays Odysseus's blind and devoted servant Eumaeus, a role that has been largely praised by critics.
  • I would go to lunch at Odeon, his favorite restaurant.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, when we think of secrecy surrounding movies, naturally we think MCU, but the amount of secrecy that went into The Odyssey is insane. While I knew everything about it was kept under wraps, I didn’t realize just how much until I heard John Leguizamo’s story about landing the script, and it’s WILD.

According to recent reports, the actor portrays Odysseus's blind and devoted servant Eumaeus, a role that has been largely praised by critics. Turns out, Christopher Nolan knew exactly what he was doing when he cast Leguizamo in the part, and he didn’t even need to eat dessert first. The actor has previously gushed about working on the movie and the amazing shooting locations, but now he’s dishing to Kevin McCarthy on his On Film podcast about the Mission Impossible-level secret keeping that went into keeping the script under wraps:.

I would go to lunch at Odeon, his favorite restaurant. So we meet. He talks about the character. First of all, he talks about his career and everything. So that was just amazing to sit with him and hear him talk about his career was incredible. And then he claims, ‘I have this role for you. It's one of the most loyal characters in Western literature.’ And I was like, ‘Wow, that's a lot to live up to.’ He goes, ‘Yes.’ And I was like, ‘I'd love to do it if you'll have me.’ He offered me the role right there before dessert.

Leguizamo’s performance as Eumaeus has been called “sublime” by critics, and it’s easy to see why Nolan thought he was the right fit. Though the actor understands there’s a certain scene in the movie that earned him some hate for “the rest of cinema history,” and if you’ve seen it, then you know what he’s referring to. The actor didn’t even know the extent of his part until he got the script, which came to him as a top secret mission fit for James Bond:.

A week later after we close the deal. I have to be home at 12:00 on a Tuesday to receive the script. Nobody else can receive it. I have to receive it. Sign for it. And it comes in a blood red color that you can only see, you know, during a full solstice. [laughter] I don't know. It's impossible to see, dude. The black ink is shiny, and the red makes it so you can't copy it. But it's hard to read. It's really difficult to read.

Perhaps Marvel needs to take some notes from Nolan. While this seems like an insane level of secrecy for a book to screen adaptation, I admire the commitment to "no spoilers." Though the journalist asked the most notable question, who delivered the script? Surely, FedEx wasn’t tasked with such a feat. Turns out one of Nolan’s personal assistants hand delivered it. However, there was still another step for him to be able to keep the confidential script:.

That's given to me, and I'm not allowed to share with anybody. My assistant had to sign an NDA.

The cloak and dagger seems to have worked as not even Tom Holland seems to have leaked anything. Additionally, Leguizamo shared that whenever Nolan made tweaks, the actor would have to turn in the old pages. This was definitely a first in his career, but one he feels was completely worth it, and I have to agree as the actor seemed to easily embody the role.

It has been revealed that it’s not easy to bring an epic of this scale to life, and it was clear from the get-go that Nolan had a vision. Now that The Odyssey hit the 2026 movie schedule over the summer, the actor can focus on a different role. Though maybe one that doesn’t come with as much secrecy? Leguizamo will reprising his role as Sid the sloth in the upcoming 2027 movie, Ice Age: Boiling Point, which is set for a February 5, 2027 release.

Industry observers note that someone should ask him if he was given the Ice Age 6 script in red. Regardless, I’d love to hear his co-stars take on the spy antics it took to keep the script out of the wrong hands.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Fresh details about Will Smith and wife Jada Pinkett Smith’s property fire in Southern California have been revealed.

It has been revealed that the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department — Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station confirmed to Us on Monday, November 23, that firefighters responded to a “structure fire” at the couple’s $42 million Calabasas home at approximately 12:04 a.m. local time.

“Security at the location reported a maintenance shed was on fire. Upon arrival, deputies saw a shed type of structure engulfed in flames,” authorities stated in a statement. “Los Angeles County Fire Department personnel arrived and extinguished the fire.”.

According to recent reports, the sheriff’s department added, “No other structures were damaged, and no one was injured. The cause of the fire was accidental.”.

Us has reached out to reps for Smith and Pinkett Smith for comment.

Page Six previously reported that a call was made to 911 around midnight local time regarding a shack on the couple’s 150-acre property catching fire but it was extinguished in the early hours on Monday.

Partial 911 audio from the incident, released by the outlet, offered more information on the situation.

“We do have a shed on fire with no spread to the brush,” a firefighter can be heard saying on the call before indicating emergency personnel were already “on scene.”.

The responding firefighter also noted that the blaze had been “downgraded to a structure.”.

The Men in Black actor, 58, and Pinkett Smith, 55, have experienced fires several times since tying the knot in December 1997.

Sources indicate that the couple, who share son Jaden, 28, and daughter Willow, 26, bought the land for their Calabasas compound in 2003. They completed their 13-bedroom estate in 2010. (Smith also shares son Trey, 34, with ex Sheree Zampino.).

According to recent reports, the property underwent a second renovation following a September 2021 fire, which broke out in the basement and led to smoke damage. The pair were later forced to evacuate during the January 2025 Palisades Fire that destroyed more than 6,000 homes, businesses and structures.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earlier this year, Steven Spielberg announced that his next movie as a director would be a Western.
  • Now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated.
  • No one's more enthused than Spielberg, though.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this year, Steven Spielberg announced that his next movie as a director would be a Western. This will be his first official crack at the most American of film genres, and that's reason enough for cinephiles to get excited.

Now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated. Factor in that Barry's book is being adapted into a script by Oscar-winner Paul Thomas Anderson, and there isn't a word in the English language to capture the utter exhilaration movie fans are feeling at this moment.

No one's more enthused than Spielberg, though. As he told Deadline:.

"It's really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite swiftly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team.".

It has been revealed that murphy will play Tom Rourke, an Irish immigrant eking out a living in Butte, Montana. He works as an assistant to a photographer and supplements his income by penning letters for illiterate miners seeking potential brides from the east. He needs the extra scratch, too, due to his alcohol and opium addictions. Tom is spiritually adrift until mail-order bride Polly Gillespie arrives in Butte. They fall fast in love, steal some money, and set what proves to be an eventful course for San Francisco.

Overall, Barry's book has echoes of Spielberg's theatrical directing debut on "The Sugarland Express," as it's about two lovers on the run from the law. But this being the late 1800s, and the pair being challenged as horseback riders, their journey isn't quite as fast-paced.

Sources indicate that kevin Barry's "The Heart in Winter" has been described as "a tragedy written as farce" (per The Guardian). Critics found it hilarious and wildly entertaining, and after his excellent work on "One Battle After Another," I can't imagine anyone more suited to a tale about a character with an opium addiction stealing a mail-order bride and heading to San Francisco than Paul Thomas Anderson. But what's most interesting to me is that this will be the first time Anderson has written an entire script for another filmmaker. He previously did rewrites on the Apple-backed "Killers of the Flower Moon" and "Napoleon" for Martin Scorsese and Ridley Scott, but he's the primary writer here.

As for Steven Spielberg, no filmmaker alive knows more about Western conventions than him, and you can rest assured he will aggressively avoid cliché. I mean, he'll be sure to keep the horizon line out of the middle of the frame, lest John Ford's eye-patched ghost haunt him for the rest of his days, but don't expect traditional Western violence of the shootout and saloon brawl variety. I haven't read the book yet, so I don't know if such scenes exist in Barry's novel, but if they do, they'll look unlike any shootout or brawl you've ever seen.

What's curious is that Spielberg went with the Montana-set "The Heart in Winter," given that he'd been talking about making a Texas Western. Texas is not Montana by a long shot, which makes me wonder if he might change the location of Barry's novel. I doubt he'd do that, so now he's cheesed off everyone in Texas who was hoping he'd make their state look sensationally epic. He'll have to make it up to them somehow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, amanda M. Castro is a Network TV writer at Collider and a New York–based journalist whose work has appeared in Newsweek, where she is an Associate Editor, and The U.S. Sun, where she previously served as a Senior Consumer Reporter.

She specializes in network television coverage, delivering sharp, thoughtful analysis of long-running procedural hits and ambitious new dramas across broadcast TV. At Collider, Amanda explores character arcs, storytelling trends, and the cultural impact of network series that keep audiences tuning in week after week.

Born and raised in Puerto Rico, Amanda is bilingual and holds a degree in Communication, Film, and Media Studies from the University of Newly introduced Haven.

Tony Soprano (James Gandolfini) is adept at making heartrending situations seem like unavoidable consequences of fate. This is one of his strengths whenever he sits in Dr. Jennifer Melfi's (Lorraine Bracco) office, where even a moment of clarity can become an opportunity to justify himself. In Season 1, Episode 7, "Down Neck," Tony gives one of his most revealing remarks about his character: "You're born into this s**t; you are what you are.".

Sources indicate that he’s discussing his father, Johnny Boy Soprano (Joseph Siravo), and the childhood that led him down the path of organized crime, almost like a family lineage. Beyond the fact that the discussion matters, he’s not just telling his childhood story. He’s in therapy because of his son, A.J. Melfi (Robert Iler) wants to know what Tony was like at his son’s age. In trying to explain his son, he starts telling stories from his own life.

It’s a fascinating choice; he understands that his childhood was shaped by things he couldn’t control. What he finds hard to understand is that A.J. is raised in a completely different environment, where Tony is already a father. The quotation suggests Tony is willing to make peace with his past, but it also shows he doesn’t consider major changes in the future.

Tony's recollections of his father are complicated, but Johnny Boy's impact is undeniable. He was a gangster whose line of work involved violence and intimidation, and Tony witnessed this world closely. He remembers the more pleasant details: his father's fondness for food, his enjoyment of life, and his fondness for people. Tony's memories of his father go beyond seeing him as the one-dimensional gangster. He also remembers his father, whom he respected, noting that what made him admirable at one point was also what made him dangerous.

Industry observers note that on the other hand, his mother, Livia (Nancy Marchand), certainly didn't provide comfort and support. Tony's connection to her was also strained, and he often struggles to remember his childhood. Besides punishment and problems, the family showed little warmth, unlike his father's, so it's understandable that Tony sees his life as shaped by circumstances and events in his early life, long before he could understand them.

The interesting point, though, is that Tony had some other options. He was bright and sporty enough to pursue a different path in life and his dreams outside the underworld and his father's operation. His view of himself, portraying himself as simply being who he is supposed to be, seems to be unrealistic.

The ironic twist in "Down Neck" is that, although Tony recounts his childhood, he does so because of A.J.'s concerns. He thinks A.J. would join the Mafia like him, but Tony realizes A.J. is a softer child who might not be cut out for the life Tony is living.

Recent findings suggest that despite his good intentions, Tony's understanding of protection is rather twisted. Meadow (Jamie-Lynn Sigler) and A.J. enjoy the luxury that comes with Tony's criminal profession. Tony believes he can give Meadow and A.J. everything that comes with his criminal career without exposing them to its sources of wealth. In other words, he thinks that he can protect and be generous at the same time while restricting the flow of information about his true life. Tony lies and deceives his kids, preparing them to accept the good things in life as well-deserved.

Recent findings suggest that A.J. is especially interesting in this case because Tony worries that his son has inherited some of his personal struggles, but he pays little attention to his parenting. A child doesn't need to inherit bad qualities to pick up bad habits by watching his parents; Tony worries about A.J.'s future but doesn't set a good example of the path he wants his kid to avoid.

Industry observers note that one reason the show remains interesting is that it takes the protagonist's mind seriously. The sessions with the therapist are a place for Tony to talk about anything he has on his mind, including his childhood, panic attacks, different reluctant feelings, and the things that still haunt him as an adult. For a time, the audience believes Tony may solve his problems through therapy; however, Melfi comes to a different conclusion. In the penultimate episode of the show, “The Blue Comet,” the therapist decides to end their relationship when she gets to know that sociopaths often use therapy to achieve their goals. This suggests that the audience has paid close attention to the sessions where the protagonist discusses challenges he may do nothing about.

At that moment, the difference between understanding oneself and wishing for improvement is clear. For several years, Tony has talked about his father, mother, and many other influences on his life. After talking about his past, he can make sense of his actions and attitudes, but that doesn’t mean he wants to take responsibility. The most annoying thing about Tony is that he doesn't completely disregard the outcome of his actions; he has enough information to feel concerned about his children’s future and understands he wouldn't want his children to grow up the way he did. Still, again and again, he tries to justify his behavior by arguing that it is simply his nature.

According to recent reports, nineteen years after the last episode of The Sopranos, that line still hurts because it sounds like a valid thought. It isn't valid, though; it is just another excuse to avoid a difficult conversation. Johnny Boy shaped Tony Soprano, but Tony has had enough time to make his own choices. His children have to pay for those choices and actions.

There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage.
  • Industry observers note that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public.
  • Recent findings suggest that but to skeptics of the U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication challenges." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

Industry observers note that that pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen.".

Recent findings suggest that but to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

According to recent reports, love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering new security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

Industry observers note that mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find latest security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be stated for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

You might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October enhancement. The company's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

Sources indicate that it's vital to understand that just about every company that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

It has been revealed that barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as promptly as possible.

The implications aren't specific to any one firm, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

Industry observers note that of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

5 Reasons Why The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Ruled The Box Office

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1643 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the biggest YA franchise in the game is back on top.
  • It has been revealed that directed once again by franchise shepherd Franchise Lawrence, "Sunrise on the Reaping" opened to a massive $120 million domestically.
  • Sources indicate that "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" looked like it was going to be a bigger hit than people realized, which proved true.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the biggest YA franchise in the game is back on top. Lionsgate released "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters over the weekend, and to say that the franchise's latest prequel film did well would be an understatement. This movie is already a huge hit for the studio and has brought the property back to its former, $100 million-plus opening weekend glory.

It has been revealed that directed once again by franchise shepherd Franchise Lawrence, "Sunrise on the Reaping" opened to a massive $120 million domestically. Internationally, the prequel bowed to $105 million, giving it a gigantic $225 million global start. It's now Lionsgate's biggest opening of 2026 overall. "Michael" ruled the box office with a $218 million global opening earlier this year, but "Sunrise on the Reaping" even managed to best the King of Pop. Now, whether or not this movie gets to the $1 billion mark like "Michael" in the long run is another question entirely, but it illustrates just how substantial this opening was.

Sources indicate that "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" looked like it was going to be a bigger hit than people realized, which proved true. It arrived right in line with bullish estimates, which climbed through the roof in the weeks leading up to its arrival. As such, it's now poised to become one of the biggest hits of the year overall.

According to recent reports, so, what went right here? How did Lionsgate manage to make such a major bet and have it pay off so spectacularly well? We're going to look at the biggest reasons why "Sunrise on the Reaping" ruled the box office on its opening weekend. Let's get into it.

The biggest thing that this movie had going for it is that it wasn't just another "Hunger Games" film or a prequel for the sake of a prequel. It was a story that hardcore fans of the franchise have been waiting a long time to see. Specifically, one involving the famed games where Haymitch Abernathy, the character played by Woody Harrelson in the previous "Hunger Games" movies, won.

It has been revealed that "Sunrise on the Reaping" pits a young Haymitch (Joseph Zada) against President Snow (Ralph Fiennes), to put it in the simplest possible terms. "Hunger Games" author Suzanne Collins wrote the book the movie is based on and, rather crucially, the novel was received very well by fans. And by most accounts, Francis Lawrence, with the help of Collins, delivered one heck of an adaptation. All of this to say, the movie promised something fans had been wanting for a hot minute and delivered the goods when the time arrived.

Industry observers note that beyond that, Jennifer Lawrence also broke her silence on her "Hunger Games" return in "Sunrise on the Reaping" ahead of the film's release, assuring that this movie was getting the original gang back together. That undoubtedly helped get more casual viewers on board who perhaps were only more interested in the original set of "Hunger Games" films. Overall, Lionsgate made the most of what this story had to offer, turning it into not just another movie but a true event within one of the biggest franchises of the last 20 years — one that demanded to be seen on the biggest screen available as soon as possible.

This is the kind of movie that hardcore fans were always going to be in the bag for, no matter what. That having been said, positive word of mouth never hurts. And while critics were, more or less, on this film's side, it worked like gangbusters for the intended audience. In the case of a long-running, beloved franchise, that is always more crucial.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" holds a decent 69% critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, as of this writing. However, it carries a stellar 94% audience score, which is near-universal praise from actual ticket buying fans. It also earned a damn good A- CinemaScore, which means word of mouth is going to be great in the weeks to come. Even though "Focker In-Law" could be a rare comedy box office hit over Thanksgiving, with Disney's "Hexed" opening as well, there should be more than enough room for this prequel to have a stellar second frame over the holiday weekend.

According to recent reports, /Film's Nina Starner wrote that "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is a prequel that "delivers" in her review. Certain critics may have been a bit softer on it, but enough of them liked it to prevent the needle from being pushed down. More importantly, fans are loudly proclaiming their love for this film, which is going to do way more to motivate viewers who might have been on the fence to check it out in the coming weeks.

Industry observers note that lionsgate doesn't always have a lot of success when playing in the substantial-budget realm, but this franchise has generally been the exception to that rule. All of "The Hunger Games" movies have been hits at the box office and, save for the very first film, they've all benefited from November releases. This ended up being an "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" situation. All the same, the studio wisely picked the perfect spot on the calendar for this prequel to thrive.

Recent findings suggest that word of mouth can't be predicted, but getting in on an otherwise fairly dead pre-Thanksgiving weekend was very wise. "Sunrise on the Reaping" got one totally unimpeded weekend to do its thing and will now benefit from a long, five-day holiday weekend over Thanksgiving. It's basically going to have nine full days of ruling the box office before taking any sort of meaningful hit.

"The Hunger Games: Mockingjay — Part 2" ruled the box office in 2015, also in November, delivering a $102 million opening weekend en route to $653 million worldwide. This latest prequel had an even bigger opening, meaning it could eclipse that global figure when all's said and done. Not to get too ahead of ourselves, but it may wind up closer to "Mockingjay — Part 1" ($766 million worldwide), if all goes well.

It has been revealed that wherever the chips fall at the end of the day, it's going to be in large part because this movie wasn't competing with a slew of other blockbusters in the midst of a crowded summer. This is the big cinematic event of choice right now and will be for at least a couple of weeks.

It certainly doesn't happen too often, but if a franchise gets it right, the breakout sequel effect can come into play. One of the best examples in history is "The Dark Knight." While Christopher Nolan's "Batman Begins" was actually a bit of a box office disappointment, pulling in a so-so $373 million worldwide, "The Dark Knight" was simply too good to be ignored and made $1 billion at a time when movies rarely ever hit that milestone.

Other examples include "John Wick"/"John Wick: Chapter 2" and "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse/"Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse." A very good first movie happened, people caught up with it after the fact, and that resulted in a much larger audience for the sequel. That brings us back to "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Despite being the sixth entry in this property, it benefited like a breakout sequel would have.

In a recent development, 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" was a surprise victor at the Thanksgiving box office, ultimately pulling in nearly $350 million worldwide on a $100 million budget. A solid result, but it wasn't nearly what the first four movies in the "Hunger Games" franchise made. However, audiences and fans caught up with it and ended up enjoying it. So, after an eight-year break, Lionsgate kind of used that first prequel to prime the pumps on this franchise, even if that wasn't the intention.

The end result is that "Songbirds & Snakes" teed up the ball for "Sunrise on the Reaping," paving the way for the film to enjoy a much, much bigger opening than its predecessor. It's not a traditional breakout sequel, but it's a breakout sequel to a prequel people enjoyed.

According to recent reports, perhaps the most important factor when it comes to playing Monday morning quarterback with the success of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" has to do with how big franchises are typically handled in Hollywood these days. Spin-offs. TV reveals. Animated entries. Theme parks. More merchandise than anyone knows what to do with.

In a recent development, that never really happened with "The Hunger Games." That's in no small part because author Suzanne Collins has a lot of say over how those affairs are handled. Even so, there was an eight-year gap between movies by the time "The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes" came around and another three years before "Sunrise on the Reaping." Neither Lionsgate nor Collins ever allowed for overexposure to get the best of this franchise. That allowed for people to be legitimately excited about this film.

Former Disney CEO Bob Iger even admitted that multiple Marvel highlights and Pixar movies going to streaming hurt those brands. The Marvel Cinematic Universe is mighty, but even fans grew tired of that. Likewise, Pixar is as good as cinema gets, yet audiences learned that they could just watch those movies at home. Meanwhile, Lionsgate has maintained discipline with the "Hunger Games" films and ensured that they remained cinematic events. Short-term gains and overdoing it would have potentially kneecapped what is now one of the studio's biggest hits in years. Hollywood could stand to learn a thing or two from this sort of execution.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Breakout star Sara Boustany is reuniting with The Body creator in an upcoming war drama movie, over a week after the Netflix show’s successful debut.

The Body is Netflix's newest psychological thriller drama following a Catholic high school dance team whose Halloween initiation ritual goes terribly wrong after one of their recruits falls into a coma. Boustany portrays Elise Zakaria, one of The Body's main characters who's introduced as the unapologetic co-captain of the Lions team. The show hails from creator and showrunner Quinn Shephard, who previously directed Zoey Deutch and Dylan O'Brien in Hulu's 2022 comedy film Not Okay. Following its release, the genre-bending series became an instant social media sensation, debuting at number three on Netflix's global top ten chart in 80 countries.

It has been revealed that over a week after winning the hearts of audiences with her breakout performance in The Body, Boustany has officially found her first movie project as lead. According to Deadline, the Lebanese-American actor has been tapped to star in Between Us and the River, an independent coming-of-age movie set in 2005 during the Iraq War. The character-driven feature reunites her with The Body creator Quinn Shephard, who has signed on as a producer. Boustany will also be joined by fellow TV standout Amélie Hoeferle, who also recently gained recognition for her fan-favorite role in the hit Prime Video show Sterling Point.

Recent findings suggest that reviews for The Body praised Boustany for her sharp comedic timing and multi-layered performance as Elise. Her magnetic chemistry with co-star Kristina Bogic has also been one of the main highlights of the show. Before landing The Body, Boustany originally had minor appearances in the 2019 shows Pen15 and Dolly Parton's Heartstrings. She also had a supporting role in 2025's Hello Beautiful movie, which featured Tricia Helfer as a famous model who gets diagnosed with breast cancer at the peak of her career.

It has been revealed that between Us and the River will center on a first-generation Iraqi-American college student and aspiring dancer, played by Boustany, who falls in love with her Mexican-American classmate. However, their relationship faces a difficult challenge when a shocking discovery leads them both to confront grief, identity, and the impact of war. Filmmaker Nika Fehmiu is directing the movie, which serves as her feature-length directorial debut. She also co-wrote the script with Baghdad Stories author Nadia Al Sultani. Before the upcoming movie, Fehmiu wrote, directed, and edited the short film Look at Me, which debuted at the Tribeca Festival.

Besides Boustany and Hoeferle, Between Us and the River will also star Alejandro Akara (Landman), Sarah Himadeh (The Last of Us), Laughton Royce (Clean Hands), and Sean Luc Rogers (Clarkston at Echo Theatre Company). It is produced by Shephard through her production banner, Ingénue, along with Fehmiu for North Wind Films. Nuer Taqa and Zoey Pressey of Radiance Pictures are also producing alongside Matt Cappetta of Planet 9 Films. Production on the upcoming coming-of-age war drama movie has already been completed.

At the time of writing, the release date for Boustany's Between Us and the River movie remains under wraps.

After a dance-team initiation mishap, a group of Catholic school girls experience prophetic visions that incite mass hysteria in their town.

The jam-packed weekend culminated with the Grand Prix itself, won in thrilling fashion by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen in the shadow of the iconic Sphere on Saturday, November 21.

Shortly before the race, Ted Lasso star and motorsports guru Hannah Waddingham gushed about the spectacle.

“I didn’t expect it to be this crazy here, which is stupid because I know that it’s Vegas,” Waddingham, 52, told Us. “I’m a real petrolhead. I sang the national anthem at the British Grand Prix. It’s my space. I love it so much.”.

Actor Michael Cimino called the experience “so sick,” saying his Formula 1 fandom bloomed by “coming to the races.”.

“I grew up in Vegas, so my first F1 was the second Vegas [Grand Prix] and that’s honestly what got me into it,” Cimino, 27, said. “It was just the excitement of seeing something like this in my hometown, which we never had when I was growing up.”.

For KPop Demon Hunters star Rei Ami – who performed at the conclusion of Saturday’s race – love of Formula can be traced back to her father, who joined her in Vegas.

It has been revealed that “When we first immigrated to the States, my dad’s first job was a mechanic,” the singer and actress, 31, explained. “I remember visiting him and seeing him in his grey charcoal cover-alls, the dirt between his nails and him coming home exhausted. He never complained. He always had the energy to take care of my sister and I, and my mom. He always helped us with our homework, took us to church every Sunday.”.

She added, “It is quite literally because of his sacrifice – him literally putting his life, his goals and his dreams to the side – that I’m allowed to stand here, live the life that I live and dream as loudly and boldly as possible. Him being a car enthusiast, I thought, ‘Let’s make sure we bring him out this year.’ At his first ever F1 experience, he’s going to see his daughter perform on top of the Paddock Club. It’s been such an unforgettable experience. It’s been so special.”.

Us had VIP access to the Paddock Club on Saturday, where the guest list was a who’s who of Hollywood, including Chris Evans, Anthony Mackie, Chris Pratt, Mark Wahlberg, Venus Williams, Adam Sandler, Lisa and more.

One of the most buzzworthy off-track story lines of the weekend was the arrival of Kim Kardashian, who was there to support her boyfriend, Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton.

Hamilton, 41, ultimately finished in 7th place, thanks largely to a crash during qualifying with teammate Charles Leclerc.

With James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exiting DC, it's unknown if the DCU will continue or if we can expect yet another reboot. However, with one chapter closing for the studio, the start of a latest might mean some long-gestating projects could get a second chance. Amid the corporate change, people have been asking about Keanu Reeves' long-discussed Constantine sequel again, and honestly, I don’t hate the possibility of seeing the 2005 movie finally get a follow-up.

In a recent development, A Constantine sequel has technically been "in the works" since 2022, and at the time, it was reported that writer Akiva Goldsman was working on the script. Director Francis Lawrence has been committed making another flick centered on Reeves' DC character, and he previously confirmed the leading man was "excited" about the idea. This is sure to be music to some fans' ears amid the major corporate shift. Jeremy Latcham, a Marvel Studios alum who worked with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy, is stepping into the role of DC Studios CEO. As a result, Gunn’s DC universe might be over, and Lawrence -- who's sympathetic to the exiting CEOs -- seems to be confident that this could open the door for a Constantine sequel.

Of course, Lawrence is also upfront about having no idea what the studio has planned. For all he knows, they could want a different John Constantine for a shared universe. With that in mind, he’s also perfectly fine if the studio want to do a fresh take and allows him to make a sequel to HIS version with Reeves. In Lawrence's mind, two iterations can co-exist.

Industry observers note that at this point, Francis Lawrence has made it clear that the project is further along than fans think, as they have a script ready to go. The only obstacle in his way is a thumbs up from the powers that be:.

It has been revealed that but again, we’ve been trying to make this for 20-something years, and there’s always been obstacles in the road to making it, and it’s not me, it’s not Keanu, it’s not Akiva. J.J. [Abrams] is on it, as well. We all want to do it. So, it’s really going to be people at Paramount, Warner, whoever’s running DC now, getting everybody on board to say, like, 'Hey, we can do a sequel of our version of Constantine.'.

Sources indicate that 2005's Constantine has earned quite the cult following. Believe it or not, Reeves wasn’t fans' first pick for the role, and that's because of how much of a departure from the comics his take on John is. The character has lived on in the live-action space since then, with Matt Ryan taking on the trench coat in 2014 for a short-lived NBC show. Ryan continued to portray Constantine in The CW’s Arrowverse and voiced the DC antihero in various animated works through 2024.

Recent findings suggest that however, a portion of fans still seem hopeful that Keanu Reeves will get another chance to play the character, and I’d love to see him back in the role. Considering Reeves' skills as an actor and his love for John, I have no doubt he can slide right back into the role. We'll have to play the waiting game on that front, though, as DC Studios has yet to reveal any upcoming looks that will follow James Gunn and Peter Safran's departures.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

In the meantime, stream Francis Lawrence's Constantine using an HBO Max subscription.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that one of his most iconic roles in recent years is the titular serial killer in Osgood Perkins' Longlegs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in his long-spanning career, Nicolas Cage has given us numerous amazing movies across various genres, including Western, drama, comedy, and superhero. The actor keeps his audience engaged by consistently delivering a range of diverse characters, be it a fictionalized version of himself in The Unbearable Weight of Massive Talent; playing a down-on-his-luck superhero, Ben Riley, in Spider-Noir; a toxic boss who also happens to be Dracula in Renfield; or playing the titular character in David O. Russell’s biographical drama Madden, his latest film.

It has been revealed that one of his most iconic roles in recent years is the titular serial killer in Osgood Perkins' Longlegs. The 2024 psychological horror-mystery, written and directed by Perkins, is among the most eerie and borderline disturbing features in the past decade. The film follows FBI Agent Lee Harker (Maika Monroe), who is assigned to an unsolved serial killer case that takes an unexpected turn, revealing evidence of the occult. Things take a darker turn when Harker discovers a personal connection to the killer and now must stop him before he strikes again.

According to recent reports, perkins created an unsettling atmosphere not by traditional jump scares, but through sensory manipulation, framing, and uncanny character design. The vast empty spaces in frames let fans check every shadow in the corner for dread. Cinematographer Andres Arochi uses muted grays, washed-out browns, and harsh winter lighting to strip away any sense of comfort. Cage played the character with an eerie feel under heavy pale prosthetics, a ragged blonde wig, and vocally gave Longlegs an erratic shift from whispers to screams to make him more unpredictable. The marketing of the film kept his evil avatar under wraps, so fans were scared firsthand in theatres.

It has been revealed that the film proved a commercial success, earning approximately $128 million worldwide on a $10 million budget. It further earned critical acclaim, garnering an 85% Rotten Tomatoes rating, with critics who collectively agreed, “Saturated in disquieting mood while leveraging a nightmarishly gonzo performance by Nicolas Cage, Longlegs is a satanic horror that effectively instills panic.” Fans who’d love to check out the feature or revisit it are in luck as Longlegs is making its way to Netflix this December, as per ComicBook. The film also features some compelling performances from Monroe as Lee Harker, Alicia Witt as her religious mother, Ruth Harker, Kiernan Shipka as Carrie Anne, among others.

Sources indicate that check out Longlegs on Netflix starting December 10. Stay tuned to Collider for more such updates.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Golden Joysticks has already weighed in on 2026's Game of the Year and The Game Awards has revealed its nominees for this year's best of the best. But one awards ceremony stands apart from the typical Game of the Year awards contest: the Steam Awards.

Recent findings suggest that on Monday, Valve opened up nominations for its fan-voted awards, which include Game of the Year and what promises to be a highly contested category: the Hall of Fame Award. That brand-latest category will pit a list of winners of the Steam Awards’ Game of the Year category from the past 10 years against each other to celebrate a decade of Valve's awards.

It has been revealed that from now until Monday, Nov. 30 at 10 a.m. PST, Steam owners can vote on the following categories, in addition to the Hall of Fame Award.

Recent findings suggest that the final nominees will be revealed, and voting for the 2026 Steam Awards will begin, on Thursday, Dec. 17. That same day, the Steam Winter Sale kicks off. That's one week to the day after The Game Awards 2026, meaning that if any PC game was slighted by that awards ceremony, Steam customers will have a chance to rebuke the TGAs voting body. (One thing that Steam Awards voters won't get to weigh in on is this year's GOTY frontrunner, Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar Games hasn't announced a PC version of the game yet.).

Industry observers note that last year's Steam Awards Game of the Year was Hollow Knight: Silksong. Other significant winners from last year's Steam Awards include Baldur’s Gate 3, Hades 2, Peak, Silent Hill f, Arc Raiders, and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the upcoming "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer indicates MCU heroes assembling for their biggest battle yet. It will also surely be one of their most profitable, given the hype around this movie. Despite Marvel Studios' well-publicized troubles of late, the Avengers' return remains highly anticipated. As such, any new revelations Marvel is willing to provide about the team-up movie are significant to say the least.

The final "Doomsday" trailer doesn't actually feature any major reveals, which is a good thing for those who prefer to keep their theater experience as pure as possible. For those who like to know as much as they can ahead of a Marvel Cinematic Universe release, however, it means much of the movie remains a mystery. (We're still no clearer on whether Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom is actually a Tony Stark variant or not, despite Marvel Studios head Kevin Feige's recent comments.) That said, the latest tease did contain several notable moments that have only served to increase the already significant hype.

Sources indicate that the new "Doomsday" trailer finally gives Cyclops the X-Men line fans were waiting for, when Marsden's hero delivers his "To me, my X-Men" rallying cry to assemble his mutants, the Avengers, Fantastic Four, and several other heroes. But beyond that tantalizing glimpse at the film's big showdown, there are several other notable moments, and lucky for you, we've gone and rounded 'em up.

Recent findings suggest that the precise plot of "Avengers: Doomsday" remains under wraps for now, but at this point, we can pretty much piece together the major beats. Previously, co-director Joe Russo told Empire that Robert Downey Jr.'s Victor Von Doom is a "father who's a victim of trauma" and that he "lost a child." That lined up with what we've seen in previous trailers, wherein Vanessa Kirby's Sue Storm/Invisible Woman talked about how Doom "used to be different" before "everything he loved was taken from him." Now, the latest "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that the Avengers themselves are responsible for it all.

In the new trailer, Chris Evans' Steve Rogers can be heard saying, "Years ago, we did what was needed to make the world right," in reference to the events of 2019's "Avengers: Endgame." He continues: "But we didn't know those choices would have consequences." It seems that Steve's choice to travel back through time to be with his lover, Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell) — and whatever the Avengers did to defeat Josh Brolin's Thanos — caused some sort of multiversal upheaval in which Doom's daughter met her, well, doom.

It has been revealed that this is why RDJ's villain tells the heroes of "Doomsday" that they've been living "stolen lives." With Steve's speech in the new trailer, it's all but certain he and the Avengers are responsible for whatever killed Doom's daughter, and likely the multiversal collapse referenced in the "Avengers Endgame: Encore" TVA scene. Turns out, Doom is the "consequence" to which Steve refers.

Sources indicate that thanks to what seemed like a hasty casting announcement prior to the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer, we knew Hailee Steinfeld's Kate Bishop would be appearing in the movie. Now, the trailer has given us our first look at the heir to the Hawkeye mantle in a very quick shot that shows her looking up at something that's clearly got her very worried. But Kate might be just one of the Young Avengers to appear in the film.

We know Scott Lang's (Paul Rudd) daughter, Cassie Lang (Kathryn Newton), is also part of "Doomsday." She indicates up briefly in the latest trailer, too, looking as concerned as Kate. Interestingly enough, both characters are in their superhero suits, which suggests they'll be joining the massive fight against Doctor Doom. That means two members of the Young Avengers will be involved in "Doomsday." Marvel Studios has yet to officially introduce these heroes as the superhero group from the comics, but has been slowly building up this new generation of Avengers over the past few years.

It has been revealed that the only likely member of the Young Avengers who hasn't appeared in trailers and is yet to be confirmed as being involved with "Doomsday" is Iman Vellani's Ms. Marvel. According to Andy Serkis, Ms. Marvel will appear in "Doomsday," but Marvel hasn't made that official. Otherwise, there are a handful of other young heroes that could show up and potentially form the Young Avengers proper in the movie itself, including Riri Williams/Ironheart (Dominique Thorne) and America Chavez (Xochitl Gomez). For now, it looks more likely than ever we'll see an official Young Avengers group unite in "Doomsday.".

According to recent reports, the upcoming "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer shows Chris Hemsworth's Thor rising from the floor surrounded by yellow lightning as opposed to his typical blue lightning. That's significant, as it all but confirms he'll be wielding a powerful new force known as the Odinforce. This power, created by the Kings of Asgard, is a major upgrade for the character, and the latest trailer appears to have shown it in action.

It has been revealed that one of the most frequently showcased "Doomsday" scenes thus far has been the moment in which Thor launches himself at Doctor Doom, only to be stopped mid-air and flung backwards by the villain's formidable force (which, as it happens, involves a Jacky Kirby-inspired energy blast from Doom). Clearly, the God of Thunder is as outmatched as the rest of his cohorts.

It has been revealed that but back when the first four teaser trailers for "Doomsday" dropped, we saw Hemsworth's hero begging his father for the "strength of the All-Fathers." Since then we've seen concept art and a "Doomsday" billboard that seemingly spoiled the fact Thor was getting a major upgrade in the form of the Odinforce. It's this force that turns his lightning yellow, and the final "Doomsday" trailer is the first time we see footage of it in action. The brief shot reveals Thor ascending in a forest, which looks to be the same forest in which he begged for the strength of the All-Fathers in the original teaser. Looks like he got his wish. Whether it will prove effective against Doom, however, remains to be seen.

According to recent reports, we got our first look at the X-Men in "Avengers: Doomsday" courtesy of the X-Men-heavy trailer back in January 2026. Since then, we've learned how the mutants might find their way to the Avengers. The film will take place during the collapse of the multiverse, whereby several "incursions" will see planets and timelines collide. These collisions are likely to be the reason for the film's major crossovers, i.e. the Fox-era X-Men and the Fantastic Four arriving on the Avengers' Earth 616. But it seems when the X-Men and Avengers first come face to face they initially clash, as evidenced by footage from prior trailers in which Yelena Belova/Black Widow (Florence Pugh) takes on Mystique (Rebecca Romijn) and Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) battles Gambit (Channing Tatum).

It has been revealed that now, however, the final "Doomsday" trailer has confirmed that Anthony Mackie's Sam Wilson/Captain America will face off against James Marsden's Scott Summers/Cyclops. The trailer shows the pair going toe-to-toe in what looks to be a pretty brutal clash, with Wilson holding Cyclops by the neck as he unleashes an optic blast. Clearly, the X-Men and Avengers ultimately manage to, as Thor puts it, "put aside their petty squabbles." But for at least a moment, the two superhero teams will be at odds in the movie, and Sam Wilson's showdown with Scott Summers looks set to be a major highlight.

The final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer reminds us of the main threat facing Earth 616 in the movie. While Doctor Doom is the major bad, the entire multiverse is collapsing, and in the latest trailer we see a brief shot that reveals two planets in the sky above New York City. The trailer also features several shots of heroes looking up at the sky, or out of windows and reacting with shock and dismay, and it's likely this planetary incursion is what has them so upset.

Industry observers note that we've known that the heroes of "Doomsday" would be dealing with multiversal collapse in the film for some time. But this is the first shot we've seen in an official trailer that shows planets on a collision course with Earth. Previously, a Dunkin' Donuts commercial gave us our best look at the threat the Avengers face in "Doomsday," with a shot showing a planet looming in the sky over Avengers Tower. But it looks as though multiple timelines/planets are set to collide with Earth based on the brief scene from this latest trailer.

Exactly which planets these are remains unclear. One may in fact be the Fox-era X-Men's world, and this cityscape view could be giving us a glimpse of their arrival in the Avengers' timeline. Either way, clearly the stakes have never been higher, as failure means the complete and utter destruction of the multiverse.

"Avengers: Doomsday" hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Voice newbie Riley Green is having a killer first season on NBC’s long-running singing competition, which is at the moment airing on the 2026 TV schedule. He easily won over the majority of the country music hopefuls during the Blind Auditions and has given the competitors excellent advice that they can continue to carry with them. But no competition is smooth sailing, and the “Don’t Mind If I Do” singer is revealing the toughest part of coaching.

It has been revealed that with the Live Shows in full swing, the country hit maker has two of Season 30’s strongest contenders, Joe Henley and Ferryn & Brinkley, still on his team. As we move ever closer to the unveiling of the winning coach and star, Green, who can presently claim the title of being one of 2026’s Sexiest Men Alive, has struggled with having to send so many talented singers home. He told People why he’s having fun during the live performances:.

I’m really excited that I’m not having to send people home. That was the toughest thing about what’s gone on so far. It was tough in the auditions because you hear these amazing stories that people have... and they’re taking off to come try to chase their dreams, and maybe they don’t get picked.

Industry observers note that nobody is ever really an overnight sensation, so The Voice’s superstar coaches absolutely understand what it’s like to chase your dreams and have setbacks along the way. I can’t imagine how agonizing it must be to know you have to send home some really talented singers. Whether you’re rookie Queen Latifah or veteran coach Adam Levine, cutting someone’s dream short never gets any easier. So, I get why Green is relieved to just sit back and enjoy the performances, and leave it up to the audience to decide who continues on and who gets cut.

In an interesting twist for Season 30, the Live Reveals have replaced the Knockouts, which happen to be Levine’s least favorite part of the competition for a very similar reason. No The Voice coach wants to have to send home talented singers, and leaving it all in America’s hands takes the pressure off the coaches. The Marshals guest star also said this about his experienceon the show:.

Industry observers note that worse than that is once you’ve worked with them and they are on your team and then having to send them home after that, I’m so sick of having to make those decisions. So I’m glad America can do it, and I’ll just try to help them along the way.

Industry observers note that one of the best parts of the reality competition show is watching how the coaches really become fans of their own team members. Kelly Clarkson has expressed her commitment to continue collaborating with Team Kelly, and I’m sure other coaches feel just as dedicated to creating such a supportive atmosphere.

I wouldn’t be surprised to see Green touring or doing special performances with his Team Riley singers, especially considering how connected he sounds like he feels with all of them. Also, it would probably go a long way toward making him feel better for those departing contestants.

The Voice Season 30 continues to air on Mondays until December 14th, when a two-hour finale will reveal who is crowned the winner. You can also watch the next day with a Peacock subscription. And Season 31’s The Voice: Celebrity is already waiting in the wings with new host Keke Palmer.

Industry News: This Creepy Twilight Zone Episode Was The First One Not Written By Rod Serling

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, no TV writer is as synonymous with their creation as Rod Serling is with "The Twilight Zone." As the show's host, he was the face of the series.
  • According to recent reports, serling wrote 92 of the 156 "Twilight Zone" episodes that aired during the show's five season run.
  • In a recent development, "Perchance to Dream" stars Richard Conte (nowadays most remembered for playing Don Barzini in "The Godfather") as Edward Hall, a man who hasn't slept for days — because he's convinced if he falls asleep, he'll die.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, no TV writer is as synonymous with their creation as Rod Serling is with "The Twilight Zone." As the show's host, he was the face of the series. In an anthology series, you can't expect to see the same actors and characters every time you tune in, so the only familiar sound to welcome you into the twilight zone was Serling's calm, sardonic voice.

According to recent reports, serling wrote 92 of the 156 "Twilight Zone" episodes that aired during the show's five season run. The first episode that did not come from a Serling script is the series' ninth episode, "Perchance to Dream," with writer Charles Beaumont self-adapting a short story he originally wrote for publication in Playboy magazine. (Now, technically, the beloved eighth "Twilight Zone" episode "Time Enough At Last," boasting one of the show's most depressing endings, was based on a short story by Lynn Venable. However, Serling wrote the teleplay.).

In a recent development, "Perchance to Dream" stars Richard Conte (nowadays most remembered for playing Don Barzini in "The Godfather") as Edward Hall, a man who hasn't slept for days — because he's convinced if he falls asleep, he'll die. But his insomnia is born of a different medical condition. Hall has a weak heart, so much so that if he experiences a significant enough shock, even in his dreams, it might literally kill him. The episode sees Hall visiting a psychiatrist, Dr. Eliot Rathmann (John Larch), and recalling how his own mind seems to be trying to knock him off a ledge with terrifying dreams.

In a recent development, the title "Perchance to Dream" comes from a soliloquy in "Hamlet," when the eponymous prince muses: "To sleep, perchance to dream." But Hamlet is talking about the sleep of death and his temptation to suicide. That makes the line a fitting, though flipped-on-its-head, title for a story about a man terrified he'll die if he falls asleep. ("Batman: The Animated Series" would later use "Perchance to Dream" as the title for star Kevin Conroy's favorite episode.).

According to recent reports, the episode is primarily set in Dr. Rathmann's skyscraper office, but peeks inside Hall's dreams to let us see his terror. The second half cuts between the office and Hall recounting his dreams of a carnival, where "everything [is] warped and twisted out of shape," and the nightmare that came closest to killing him. A cat-eyed woman named Maya (Suzanne Lloyd) leads Hall down a haunted trail, packed with monstrous animatronics, and then onto a roller coaster.

According to recent reports, maya's feline coding marks her as a predator, toying with Hall like a terrified mouse trying to escape her claws. Watching the episode now, it feels like "A Nightmare on Elm Street" with a femme fatale instead of a knife-handed slasher. The carnival scenes use Dutch angles and foggy camera filters feel extra unnerving and wrong. Combined with the Halloween aesthetic and Maya's cutting laughter, the dream lives up to the nightmare that Hall described.

Charles Beaumont remained one of most prolific "Twilight Zone" writers. During the second season, he self-adapted his spooky short story "The Howling Man," helping turn it into one of the scariest "Twilight Zone" episodes ever. But "Perchance to Dream" first proved that Beaumont could makes trips to the Twilight Zone genuinely terror-inducing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that katrina joined ScreenRant as a news writer in 2024, covering box office, expert interviews, exclusives, and latest releases. Her work has appeared in CBR, All About Jazz, Rising Artists, and numerous other publications. She has an MFA in Creative Writing and has published more than 20 books. She at the moment writes for ScreenRant’s movie features team.

Hexed marks Disney's last animated movie in 2026. From the directors behind Moana 2 and Wish, the fresh fantasy movie puts a new spin on the "Chosen One" trope and tells a story about a daughter and mother healing their relationship with each other while discovering and rediscovering their relationships with magic.

In a recent development, hailee Steinfeld voices the protagonist of Hexed, Billie Doe, a misunderstood and unconventional teenager, while Rashida Jones voices Billie's mother, Alice, who is a witch herself. Jodie Foster takes on the role of the villain and queen of the witches in the realm of Hexe.

Hexed has many charismatic but refreshing features that resemble the world of Harry Potter. From a talking book to a pen that's alive and a three-eyed cat, the Disney film builds a whimsical world that fans can immerse themselves in.

The trailer for Hexed offers fans a glimpse of what they can expect from the upcoming fantasy movie. Much like Harry Potter and Alice in Wonderland, where the magical world remains separate and hidden from the ordinary world, Billie can only access the realm of Hexe through a magical portal.

According to recent reports, like Harry Potter, Billie is regarded as a problematic teenager. She's different from other kids, and when the bracelet that suppresses her power accidentally falls off, her magic creates an incident that leads to her being expelled from school. However, the exact thing that makes her different turns out to be the very thing that makes her special.

Billie discovers a world where witches like her live in peace and harmony, a world where she truly belongs, which also brings forth mysteries and secrets about her own family.

In a recent development, the new Disney movie tackles a similar theme to Harry Potter, where the protagonist, who always feels displaced and isolated from the world she grew up in, finds belonging through adventures, friendships, and being embraced for who she truly is. Hexed also doesn't stop at the existing winning formula. It adds a twist to a story about magic.

Even before Hexed, Disney movies such as Turning Red and Encanto had already experimented with the multi-generation angle, placing magic in the context of family, tradition, and culture. Hexed further puts its emphasis on a parent-child relationship, which serves as a spiritual theme in Harry Potter.

Harry Potter wouldn't have survived Voldemort as a baby without his mother sacrificing herself to protect him. He also inherited his father's talent for Quidditch. Even though Harry's parents aren't physically present in the story, they still play a huge part in the story. Part of Harry's journey in the magic world is about learning more about his parents and encountering people who knew them.

Lily and James' presence is deeply woven into the series' most powerful moments. Even though they are deceased, their spirits are carried throughout the series. From the Mirror of Erised to Snape's Patronus taking the same form as Lily's and the final battle, where their spirits stand by Harry while he faces Voldemort, they are always with Harry.

Hexed doesn't miss the opportunity with Alice and Billie either. The movie places an emphasis on their relationship with each other as Alice follows her daughter and travels to Hexe. She also fights alongside Billie to defeat the villain.

Many of the animated coming-of-age movies focus on the protagonist's journey of growing up. What makes Hexed unique is that it breaks the trend of making teenage adventures only about friendship or being on their own and places Alice's motherhood journey at the forefront alongside Billie's adventure and reveals them finding their way back to each other.

Impulsive teenager Billie discovers that her unusual abilities are actually magic, sending her from suburban life into Hexe, a vast hidden realm of witches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding Port Gelhorn's missing tourists and the serial killer in Grand Theft Auto 6 takes you on a twisted journey around the town, one with few guideposts and a lot of chances to get stuck. It's a macabre scavenger hunt with only a few pictures and knowledge of the surrounding area to go by, though the reward at the end is comparatively small. This is a quest where the storytelling, more than anything else, is the reward.

Below, we explain where to find Gelhorn's missing tourists in GTA 6 and complete the serial killer side mission.

Sources indicate that you'll first come across this exploration mission in the Starlet Motel office after Chapter 2 starts. Lucia can examine a set of missing persons posters on the wall next to Linda's desk. There's a tip line with a number to call, but it just takes you to a voice mailbox.

And that's the only hint to go off of, as the poster info gives you no clues and nowhere to look. There might be other clues hidden somewhere around town, but we didn't find them. Instead, we stumbled across the quest's starting location by accident. It's an old bunker-like warehouse across the street from Moses' garage, next to the scooter store. You can approach the front for a prompt to open the door, but it won't work. Walk down the right side of the warehouse, and look for a hole at the base. Crawl inside.

Industry observers note that despite how creepy the location is, there's nothing inside to harm you, though there is a jump scare midway through. Enter the red room and the trophy room beyond it, and interact with the photos there. You'll see locations showing each of the missing tourists, and these photos are stored in your phone gallery if you want to view them later. The quest prompt changes in the map menu, too, with a new prompt for each photo.

You can track them in any order. We're just listing them in the order we found them. We recommend tackling this part of the quest during the day, just so it's easier to make out landmarks.

Recent findings suggest that the junkyard is where you'll find Susanne Keeble, and it's next to the Pay 'n' Spray shop in central Gelhorn. You're looking for a pink car, and if you're having trouble finding it, activate focus mode. The car will stand out as the only interactable object in the area. Report the body to the tip line after you find it.

In a recent development, donald Miller's body is out at Wild Hog Point, the marshes outside Port Gelhorn. Head toward the tree with no leaves near the center of the marsh, and look in the water nearby to find a car. Interact with it, report the body, and move on. Someone picks up the line this time.

Industry observers note that patrick Murray is the final tourist, and his body is in a trailer at the far north end of Port Gelhorn in an abandoned trailer park near a water tower. The trailer in question is the blue one. Head inside, and pull up the floorboards near the door to discover Murray's body. The clipping in the trophy room mentioned a reward for information about him, though, for reasons you'll soon discover, the tip line operator isn't ready to pay out.

The tip line man asks you to return to the warehouse after finding the third body, and the quest can change depending on whether you go alone or with your partner. We played as Jason and went with Lucia, though who takes the lead doesn't matter. Your partner stays outside, and tense events unfold inside, after which the culprit dies and the quest ends. You can grab the killer's glasses as a unique "found" accessory for Jason if you want.
